Statements and instructions Declarative knowledge is statements of fact. Imperative knowledge is a recipe or “how-to”. A fact describes what is true. A recipe specifies steps to follow. MIT OCW 6.0001 / Lecture 1  /  1

A recipe for the square root of x 1. Start with a guess, g. 2. If g*g is close enough to x, stop and say g is the answer. 3. Otherwise make a new guess by averaging g and x/g. 4. Using the new guess, repeat until close enough. MIT OCW 6.0001 / Lecture 1  /  2

The parts of an algorithm A sequence of simple steps. A flow of control that specifies when each step is executed. A means of determining when to stop. These three parts form an algorithm. MIT OCW 6.0001 / Lecture 1  /  3
